output.title: Spot survivorship bias before it warps your sample
output.body:
Survivorship bias shows up when you only see what made it through. In a small business, that can mean learning from successful orders, active customers, or clean invoices while the failed cases, silent prospects, or messy edge cases stay out of view. Then the sample looks reassuring, but the decision was made on missing evidence.

The practical question is simple: what decision are you making from samples right now, and how would you know early if it was going to fail? That is the point where AI may help, but only if the data is already observable. If your samples are scattered, anecdotal, or need judgment to interpret, AI alone is not the answer.

One useful next step is manual: take one recent decision, write down the sample you used, what was missing, and what would have changed if the missing cases had been visible up front. Do that before you reach for a tool. Once the gap is clear, you can decide whether a spreadsheet check, a manual review, or an AI-assisted workflow is the better investment.
